citation.title: A Class of Unbiased Estimators of the Average Treatment Effect in Randomized Experiments

standing_assumptions:
Finite-population, design-based potential-outcomes setting (the Neyman-Rubin model): potential outcomes and covariates are fixed and the only randomness is the assignment of units to treatment and control. Transcribed from the page images.

(S1) Section 3, pp. 137-138 (PDF pp. 3-4): 'Define a binary treatment indicator $T_i$ for units $i = 1,2,\ldots,N$ such that $T_i = 1$ when unit $i$ receives the treatment and $T_i = 0$ otherwise. If the stable unit treatment value assumption [16] holds, let $Y_{1i}$ be the potential outcome if unit $i$ is exposed to the treatment, and let $Y_{0i}$ be the potential outcome if unit $i$ is not exposed to the treatment. The observed outcome $Y_i$ may be expressed as a function of the potential outcomes and the treatment: $Y_i = T_iY_{1i} + (1-T_i)Y_{0i}$. [1] The causal effect of the treatment on unit $i$, $\tau_i$, is defined as the difference between the two potential outcomes for unit $i$: $\tau_i \equiv Y_{1i} - Y_{0i}$. [2] The ATE, denoted by $\Delta$, is defined as the average value of $\tau_i$ for all units $i$. In the Neyman-Rubin model, the only random component is the allocation of units to treatment and control groups.' Eq. [3]: $\Delta = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\tau_i}{N} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(Y_{1i}-Y_{0i})}{N} = \frac{1}{N}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{N}Y_{1i} - \sum_{i=1}^{N}Y_{0i}\right] = \frac{1}{N}\left[Y_1^T - Y_0^T\right]$, 'where $Y_1^T$ is the sum of the potential outcomes if in the treatment condition and $Y_0^T$ is the sum of potential outcomes if in the control condition.' Eq. [4]: $\widehat{\Delta} = \frac{1}{N}\left[\widehat{Y_1^T} - \widehat{Y_0^T}\right]$, 'where $\widehat{Y_1^T}$ is the estimated sum of potential outcomes under treatment and $\widehat{Y_0^T}$ is the estimated sum of potential outcomes under control.' Footnote 2 (p. 138): 'This assumption is made without loss of generality; multiple discrete treatments (or equivalently, some units not being sampled into either treatment or control) are easily accommodated in this framework. All instances of $(1 - T_i)$ in the text may be replaced by $C_i$, an indicator variable for whether or not unit $i$ receives the control, with one exception to be noted in Section 6.'

(S2) p. 138 (PDF p. 4): 'Formally, the bias of an estimator is the difference between the expected value of the estimator and the true parameter of interest; an estimator is unbiased if this difference is equal to zero. If the estimators $\widehat{Y_0^T}$ and $\widehat{Y_1^T}$ are unbiased, the corresponding estimator of $\Delta$ is also unbiased since $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\Delta}] = \frac{1}{N}\left[\mathrm{E}[\widehat{Y_1^T}] - \mathrm{E}[\widehat{Y_0^T}]\right] = \frac{1}{N}\left[Y_1^T - Y_0^T\right] = \Delta$.' [5]

(S3) Section 4, p. 138 (PDF p. 4): 'Define $N$ as the number of units in the study, $\pi_{1i}$ as the probability that unit $i$ is selected into treatment, and $\pi_{0i}$ as the probability that unit $i$ is selected into control. We assume that, $\forall i$, $\pi_{1i} > 0$ and $\pi_{0i} > 0$, or that there is a nonzero probability that each unit will be selected into treatment and that there is a nonzero probability that each unit will be selected into control. (When all units are assigned to either treatment or control, $\pi_{0i} + \pi_{1i} = 1$.)'

(S4) Section 5, pp. 140-141 (PDF pp. 6-7): eqs. [13]-[14], $\widehat{Y_1^{T*}} = \sum_{i=1}^{N}\left[T_i\frac{Y_{1i}}{\pi_{1i}} - T_i\frac{f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{1i}} + f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})\right]$ and $\widehat{Y_0^{T*}} = \sum_{i=1}^{N}\left[(1-T_i)\frac{Y_{0i}}{\pi_{0i}} - (1-T_i)\frac{f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{0i}} + f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})\right]$, 'where $f(.)$ is a predetermined real-valued function of pretreatment covariate vector $\mathbf{X_i}$ and of parameter vector $\theta_{\mathbf{i}}$'; eq. [15], $\widehat{\Delta_G} = \frac{1}{N}\left(\widehat{Y_1^{T*}} - \widehat{Y_0^{T*}}\right)$; eq. [16], $\widehat{\Delta_G} = \widehat{\Delta_{HT}} - \frac{1}{N}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}T_i\frac{f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{1i}} - \sum_{i=1}^{N}(1-T_i)\frac{f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{0i}}\right)$.

(S5) Section 6.1, p. 143 (PDF p. 9): '$\pi_{1i1j}$ is the probability that units $i$ and $j$ are jointly included in the treatment group'; '$\pi_{0i0j}$ is the probability that units $i$ and $j$ are jointly included in the control group'; '$\pi_{1i0j}$ is the joint probability that unit $i$ will be in the treatment group and unit $j$ will be in the control group.'

(S6) Section 6.2, pp. 143-144 (PDF pp. 9-10): 'When $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$ is constant, we may simply redefine the outcome variable, $U_i = Y_i - f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$. It follows that $U_{0i} = Y_{0i} - f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$ and $U_{1i} = Y_{1i} - f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$.' and 'As we proceed, for notational clarity, we use $Y_i$ as the outcome measure, noting that the variances derived will also apply to the generalized difference estimator if $U_i$ is substituted for $Y_i$ (along with both associated potential outcomes) and $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$ is constant.'

(S7) Section 6.3, pp. 144-145 (PDF pp. 10-11), cluster totals: 'Note that if, for some units $i,j$, $\Pr(T_i \neq T_j) = 0$, then the total estimators may be equivalently rewritten. Define $K_k \in \mathbf{K}$ as the set of unit indices $i$ that satisfy $T_i = T'_k$, where $T'_k$ is indexed over all $|\mathbf{K}|$ unique random variables in $\{T_i : i = (1,2,\ldots,N)\}$. Define $\pi'_{1k}$ as the value of $\pi_{1i}, \forall i \in K_k$, $\pi'_{0k}$ as the value of $\pi_{0i}, \forall i \in K_k$. Joint probabilities $\pi'_{1k1l}$, $\pi'_{1k0l}$, and $\pi'_{0k0l}$ are defined analogously.' With '$Y'_k = \sum_{i \in K_k} Y_i$' (p. 144) and '$Y'_{1k} = \sum_{i \in K_k} Y_{1i}$ and $Y'_{0k} = \sum_{i \in K_k} Y_{0i}$' (p. 145). The sums over clusters run over $k = 1,\ldots,M$.

(S8) Section 6.4, p. 145 (PDF p. 11): 'Our goal is now to derive conservative variance estimators: although not unbiased, these estimators are guaranteed to have a nonnegative bias.' Footnote 7: 'Although the variance estimator is nonnegatively biased, the associated standard errors may not be (due to Jensen's inequality) and any particular draw may be above or below the true value of the variance due to sampling variability.'

Reading conventions used in every target below (they follow from (S1)-(S7) in the two-arm case that the paper works in; stated here for the formalizer and flagged as conventions, not quotations): the assignment vector $(T_1,\ldots,T_N)$ has an arbitrary probability distribution on $\{0,1\}^N$ (a finite sample space), and all expectations, variances and covariances are taken over it; every unit is assigned to treatment or control, so $\pi_{1i} = \Pr(T_i = 1)$, $\pi_{0i} = \Pr(T_i = 0) = 1 - \pi_{1i}$, $\pi_{1i1j} = \Pr(T_i = 1, T_j = 1)$, $\pi_{0i0j} = \Pr(T_i = 0, T_j = 0)$, $\pi_{1i0j} = \Pr(T_i = 1, T_j = 0)$, hence $\pi_{1i1i} = \pi_{1i}$, $\pi_{0i0i} = \pi_{0i}$ and $\pi_{1i0i} = 0$, and likewise for the primed cluster quantities; the clusters $K_1,\ldots,K_M$ partition $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, $T_i = T'_k$ for every $i \in K_k$, and distinct clusters have distinct indicators, $\Pr(T'_k \neq T'_l) > 0$ for $k \neq l$; every double sum over $k, l$ (or $i, j$) is over ordered pairs; 'the sharp null hypothesis of no treatment effect whatsoever' means $Y_{1i} = Y_{0i}$ for every unit $i$.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Table 2, column G (Linear) (rows SE, RMSE, Var, E[Var-hat], SE, RMSE) and column FE (Cov.) (rows E[Delta-hat], Bias, SE, RMSE, Var), as printed, set against the population of Table 1 and the estimators of Section 7.1
canonical_claim.location: Table 2, p. 149 (PDF p. 15); Table 1, p. 147 (PDF p. 13); Section 7.1, p. 148 (PDF p. 14)
canonical_claim.statement:
Printed statement refuted. Table 2 (p. 149), 'ATE and variance estimator properties for numerical example', column G (Linear): $\Delta = 0.000$; $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\Delta}] = 0.000$; Bias $= 0.000$; SE $= 0.162$; RMSE $= 0.162$; Var $= 0.026$; $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}] = 0.026$; Bias $= 0.000$; SE $= 0.007$; RMSE $= 0.007$. Column FE (Cov.): $0.000$; $-0.012$; $-0.012$; $0.191$; $0.191$; $0.036$; $0.031$; $-0.005$; $0.011$; $0.012$. The table is presented as the properties of the estimators for the population of Table 1 'over all 90 possible randomizations' (p. 148).

Refutation by exact enumeration for the population printed in Table 1.
(A) G (Linear). The OLS fit of $Y$ on an intercept and $X$ over the ten units of block 2 is $1/4 + X/8$, and over the six units of block 1 it is $70/93 + X/31$; so $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}}) = 1/4 + X_i/8$ for units in block 1 and $70/93 + X_i/31$ for units in block 2. The cluster totals of $U_i = Y_i - f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$ are $(1,\ 7/8,\ 1/4,\ -1/2,\ -15/31,\ 19/93,\ 1/3,\ -76/93,\ -76/93,\ -79/93)$ for clusters 1 to 10. Over the 90 assignments: $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\Delta_G}] = 0$; $\mathrm{Var}(\widehat{\Delta_G}) = 38307/634880$ ($\approx 0.0603374$; square root $\approx 0.2456367$); $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_G)] = 38307/634880$; $\mathrm{Var}(\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_G)) = 2400328658503/15687787688755200$ (square root $\approx 0.0123696$). Hence the printed entries are false for the printed population: $38307/634880 > 0.0265$, so neither Var nor $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}]$ rounds to $0.026$; $38307/634880 > 0.1625^2$, so neither SE nor RMSE rounds to $0.162$; and $2400328658503/15687787688755200 > 0.0075^2$, so neither the SE nor the RMSE of the variance estimator rounds to $0.007$.
(B) FE (Cov.). For each of the 90 assignments let $\widehat{\Delta}_{FE(Cov)}$ be the coefficient on $T_i$ in the ordinary least squares regression of $Y_i$ on an intercept, $T_i$, the indicator of block 2 and $X_i$ (16 observations). Then $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\Delta}_{FE(Cov)}] \approx -0.0139874$ (strictly between $-0.0145$ and $-0.0135$, so it does not round to $-0.012$) and $\mathrm{Var}(\widehat{\Delta}_{FE(Cov)}) \approx 0.0777347$ (strictly between $0.0775$ and $0.0785$, so it does not round to $0.036$; its square root $\approx 0.2788094$ does not round to $0.191$).
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Table 1 (p. 147, PDF p. 13), columns Unit, Block, Cluster, $Y_{1i}$, $Y_{0i}$, $X_i$, $\pi_{1i}$: (1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 4, 2/4); (2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 2/4); (3, 1, 2, 1, 1, 4, 2/4); (4, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2/4); (5, 1, 3, 1, 1, 4, 2/4); (6, 1, 4, 0, 0, 2, 2/4); (7, 2, 5, 1, 1, 4, 2/6); (8, 2, 5, 1, 1, 1, 2/6); (9, 2, 5, 0, 0, 2, 2/6); (10, 2, 6, 1, 1, 5, 2/6); (11, 2, 6, 1, 1, 4, 2/6); (12, 2, 7, 1, 1, 1, 2/6); (13, 2, 7, 1, 1, 4, 2/6); (14, 2, 8, 0, 0, 2, 2/6); (15, 2, 9, 0, 0, 2, 2/6); (16, 2, 10, 0, 0, 3, 2/6). Design (p. 147, PDF p. 13): 'Consider a hypothetical randomized experiment run on 16 individuals organized into 10 clusters across two blocks. A single prognostic covariate $\mathbf{X}$ is available, and two clusters in each block are randomized into treatment, with the others randomized into control.' p. 148 (PDF p. 14): 'Note that we have assumed no treatment effect whatsoever. We may now assess the performance of both (average) treatment effect estimators and associated variance estimators, by computing the estimated ATE and variance over all 90 possible randomizations.' So the assignment is uniform on the $\binom{4}{2}\binom{6}{2} = 90$ choices of two of clusters 1-4 and two of clusters 5-10, $\pi'_{1k} = 1/2$ for clusters 1-4 and $1/3$ for clusters 5-10, and $Y_i = Y_{1i} = Y_{0i}$. Section 7.1, p. 148: 'In all cases, we use the general formulations in $\widehat{\Delta_G}$ and $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_G)$, but vary the form and parameters of $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$. In the "G (Prior)" specification, we set $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}}) = 0.5$ ... In the "G (Linear)" specification, $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}}) = \beta_{0b} + \beta_{1b}X_i$, where $b$ indicates the block of the unit. For units in block 1, we estimate $\beta_{01}$ and $\beta_{11}$ from an OLS regression of $Y_i$ on the covariate (including an intercept) using only units in block 2. $\beta_{02}$ and $\beta_{12}$ are similarly estimated from an OLS regression using only units in block 1. ... In the "G (Logit)" specification, $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}}) = 1 - 1/(1 + \exp(\beta_{0b} + \beta_{1b}X_i))$. $\beta_{01}$ and $\beta_{11}$ are now derived from a logistic regression using only the units in block 2 (and vice versa for $\beta_{02}$ and $\beta_{12}$).' Rows of Table 2, in order: $\Delta$; $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\Delta}]$, Bias, SE, RMSE (of the ATE estimator); Var; $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}]$, Bias, SE, RMSE (of the variance estimator). All are moments over the 90 equiprobable assignments (population moments, dividing by 90). The estimator: eq. [16] (equivalently eq. [25]), $\widehat{\Delta_G} = \widehat{\Delta_{HT}} - \frac{1}{N}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}T_i\frac{f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{1i}} - \sum_{i=1}^{N}(1-T_i)\frac{f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{0i}}\right)$, and the variance estimator eq. [35] applied to the residual cluster totals (in this design all $\pi'_{1k1l}$, $\pi'_{0k0l}$, $\pi'_{1k0l}$ with $k \neq l$ are positive, so every $\varepsilon$ is $0$ and the sums over zero joint probabilities are empty): $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT}) = \frac{1}{N^2}\sum_{k=1}^{M}\Bigg[T'_k\left(\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{1k}}\right)^2 + (1-T'_k)\left(\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{0k}}\right)^2 + \sum_{l\neq k}\Bigg(\frac{T'_kT'_l}{\pi'_{1k1l}+\varepsilon_{1k1l}}(\pi'_{1k1l}-\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{1l})\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{1k}}\frac{Y'_l}{\pi'_{1l}} + \frac{(1-T'_k)(1-T'_l)}{\pi'_{0k0l}+\varepsilon_{0k0l}}(\pi'_{0k0l}-\pi'_{0k}\pi'_{0l})\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{0k}}\frac{Y'_l}{\pi'_{0l}} - 2\frac{T'_k(1-T'_l)}{\pi'_{1k0l}+\varepsilon_{1k0l}}(\pi'_{1k0l}-\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{0l})\frac{Y'_kY'_l}{\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{0l}}\Bigg) + \sum_{\forall l:\pi'_{1k1l}=0}\left(T'_k\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{2\pi'_{1k}} + T'_l\frac{(Y'_l)^2}{2\pi'_{1l}}\right) + \sum_{\forall l:\pi'_{0k0l}=0}\left((1-T'_k)\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{2\pi'_{0k}} + (1-T'_l)\frac{(Y'_l)^2}{2\pi'_{0l}}\right)\Bigg]$, with $N = 16$, $M = 10$ and $Y'_k$ replaced by $\sum_{i\in K_k}U_i$. FE (Cov.), p. 148: 'ordinary least squares, holding fixed effects for randomization strata (the "FE" estimator) ... Similarly, we also use the fixed effects estimator including the covariate $\mathbf{X}$ (the "FE (Cov.)" estimator) in the regression.'
canonical_claim.note: The validator's evidence is an exact recomputation (evidence_type exact_counterexample). Part (A) is exact rational arithmetic and was recomputed independently when this target was fixed (fits, residual totals, 38307/634880, and the variance of the variance estimator). Part (B) is rational in principle (the exact fractions have denominators of about a hundred digits; see moments.json next to the derivation), so the target states it by rounding intervals; it was recomputed in exact arithmetic for the ATE rows. The G (Logit) column is P026-T14. The RE (Cov.) column is not established (the cited lme4 version could not be run) and the FE (Cov.) variance-estimator rows depend on a small-sample correction the paper does not state; neither is part of this target.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Table 2, columns G (Linear) and FE (Cov.), corrected for the population printed in Table 1
canonical_claim.location: Table 2, p. 149 (PDF p. 15); Table 1, p. 147 (PDF p. 13); Section 7.1, p. 148 (PDF p. 14)
canonical_claim.statement:
Corrected statement (Table 1 and Section 7.1 kept as printed; the entries of Table 2 replaced). For the population of Table 1 and the 90 equiprobable assignments:
(a) G (Linear): with $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}}) = 1/4 + X_i/8$ for units in block 1 and $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}}) = 70/93 + X_i/31$ for units in block 2 (the opposite-block OLS fits), $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\Delta_G}] = 0 = \Delta$; $\mathrm{Var}(\widehat{\Delta_G}) = 38307/634880$; $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_G)] = 38307/634880$ (the variance estimator of eq. [35] is exactly unbiased here); $\mathrm{Var}(\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_G)) = 2400328658503/15687787688755200$. To three decimals the column reads, in the row order of Table 2, $0.000$; $0.000$; $0.000$; $0.246$; $0.246$; $0.060$; $0.060$; $0.000$; $0.012$; $0.012$ (that is, $0.2455 \leq \sqrt{38307/634880} < 0.2465$, $0.0595 \leq 38307/634880 < 0.0605$ and $0.0115 \leq \sqrt{2400328658503/15687787688755200} < 0.0125$).
(b) FE (Cov.), ATE rows: with $\widehat{\Delta}_{FE(Cov)}$ the OLS coefficient on $T_i$ in the regression of $Y_i$ on an intercept, $T_i$, the indicator of block 2 and $X_i$, the rows $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\Delta}]$, Bias, SE, RMSE, Var read $-0.014$; $-0.014$; $0.279$; $0.279$; $0.078$ (that is, $-0.0145 < \mathrm{E}[\widehat{\Delta}_{FE(Cov)}] < -0.0135$, $0.0775 < \mathrm{Var}(\widehat{\Delta}_{FE(Cov)}) < 0.0785$, and both $\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}}$ and $\sqrt{\mathrm{Var} + \mathrm{E}[\widehat{\Delta}_{FE(Cov)}]^2}$ lie in $[0.2785, 0.2795)$).
(c) The qualitative comparison survives with a smaller margin: $\sqrt{38307/634880} < \sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(\widehat{\Delta}_{FE(Cov)}) + \mathrm{E}[\widehat{\Delta}_{FE(Cov)}]^2}$, i.e. the RMSE of G (Linear) ($\approx 0.2456$) is below that of FE (Cov.) ($\approx 0.2792$).
(d) The columns that do not use $X$ are unchanged; in particular, for HT ($f = 0$) and G (Prior) ($f = 0.5$) the estimator is unbiased and $\mathrm{Var} = \mathrm{E}[\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C] = 353/1920$ and $233/2560$ respectively, which round to the printed $0.184$ and $0.091$.

canonical_claim.statement:
Corrected statement. Setting (Section 6.3 with the standing assumptions): $M$ clusters with assignment indicators $T'_1,\ldots,T'_M \in \{0,1\}$ following an arbitrary probability distribution on $\{0,1\}^M$; $\pi'_{1k} = \Pr(T'_k = 1) > 0$ and $\pi'_{0k} = \Pr(T'_k = 0) = 1 - \pi'_{1k} > 0$ for every $k$; $\pi'_{1k1l} = \Pr(T'_k = 1, T'_l = 1)$, $\pi'_{0k0l} = \Pr(T'_k = 0, T'_l = 0)$, $\pi'_{1k0l} = \Pr(T'_k = 1, T'_l = 0)$; fixed real cluster totals $Y'_{1k}$ and $Y'_{0k}$; observed total $Y'_k = T'_kY'_{1k} + (1 - T'_k)Y'_{0k}$; $N \geq 1$ the number of units; $\widehat{Y_1^T} = \sum_{k=1}^{M} T'_kY'_k/\pi'_{1k}$, $\widehat{Y_0^T} = \sum_{k=1}^{M}(1 - T'_k)Y'_k/\pi'_{0k}$ and $\widehat{\Delta}_{HT} = (\widehat{Y_1^T} - \widehat{Y_0^T})/N$. All double sums are over ordered pairs. Write $Z_{11} = \{(k,l) : k 
eq l,\ \pi'_{1k1l} = 0\}$, $Z_{00} = \{(k,l) : k 
eq l,\ \pi'_{0k0l} = 0\}$ and $Z_{10} = \{(k,l) : k 
eq l,\ \pi'_{1k0l} = 0\}$.

(a) (First display of Appendix E, eq. [30]; holds in every design of the setting.) $\mathrm{Cov}\left(\widehat{Y_1^T},\widehat{Y_0^T}ight) = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{l

Printed statement refuted. Appendix E, p. 152: '$\mathrm{Cov}_C\left(\widehat{Y_1^T},\widehat{Y_0^T}\right)$ may be estimated without bias:' $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{Y_1^T}) = \sum_{k=1}^{M}T'_k(1-\pi'_{1k})\left(\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{1k}}\right)^2 + \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{l\neq k:\pi'_{1k1l}>0}\frac{T'_kT'_l}{\pi'_{1k1l}}(\pi'_{1k1l}-\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{1l})\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{1k}}\frac{Y'_l}{\pi'_{1l}} - \sum_{k=1}^{M}T'_k\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{2\pi'_{1k}} - \sum_{k=1}^{M}(1-T'_k)\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{2\pi'_{0k}}$, 'by $\mathrm{E}[T'_k(1-T'_l)] = \pi'_{1k0l}$, $\mathrm{E}[T'_k] = \pi'_{1k}$, $\mathrm{E}[1-T'_k] = \pi'_{0k}$ and eq. [1].' That is, the claim that the expectation of the displayed expression equals $\mathrm{Cov}_C\left(\widehat{Y_1^T},\widehat{Y_0^T}\right)$ of eq. [43].

Counterexample (the validator's; exact arithmetic; no joint probability of distinct clusters is zero). $N = M = 4$ with $K_k = \{k\}$; exactly two of the four clusters are treated, each of the six subsets with probability $1/6$; $(Y'_{1k})_{k=1}^{4} = (Y'_{0k})_{k=1}^{4} = (1,2,4,7)$ (sharp null). Then $\pi'_{1k} = \pi'_{0k} = 1/2$ and, for $k \neq l$, $\pi'_{1k1l} = \pi'_{0k0l} = 1/6$ and $\pi'_{1k0l} = 1/3$. On the treated subsets $\{1,2\}$, $\{1,3\}$, $\{1,4\}$, $\{2,3\}$, $\{2,4\}$, $\{3,4\}$ the displayed expression takes the values $-68$, $-52$, $2$, $-62$, $-20$, $-52$, so its expectation is $-42$; whereas $\mathrm{Cov}_C\left(\widehat{Y_1^T},\widehat{Y_0^T}\right) = -28$ (eq. [43]) and $\mathrm{Cov}\left(\widehat{Y_1^T},\widehat{Y_0^T}\right) = -28$. Eq. [34] takes the values $-37$, $-25$, $-22$, $-22$, $-25$, $-37$ on the same subsets, with expectation $-28$. The displayed expression is not an unbiased estimator of the quantity named on its left-hand side either: $\mathrm{Var}(\widehat{Y_1^T}) = \mathrm{Var}_C(\widehat{Y_1^T}) = 28$.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 6.3, unnumbered display rewriting the HT estimator of the treatment total over cluster totals, with pi_{1i} in the first sum (printed pi_i), and the companion display for the control total
canonical_claim.statement: Corrected statement. Under the cluster notation of Section 6.3 (the sets $K_1,\ldots,K_M$ partition $\{1,\ldots,N\}$; $T_i = T'_k$, $\pi_{1i} = \pi'_{1k}$ and $\pi_{0i} = \pi'_{0k}$ for every $i \in K_k$; $Y'_k = \sum_{i\in K_k}Y_i$): $\widehat{Y^T_{1,HT}} = \sum_{i=1}^{N}\frac{1}{\pi_{1i}}T_iY_i = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{i\in K_k}\frac{1}{\pi_{1i}}T_iY_i = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{i\in K_k}\frac{1}{\pi'_{1k}}T'_kY_i = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\frac{1}{\pi'_{1k}}T'_k\sum_{i\in K_k}Y_i = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\frac{1}{\pi'_{1k}}T'_kY'_k$, 'where $Y'_k = \sum_{i\in K_k}Y_i$. And, similarly,' $\widehat{Y^T_{0,HT}} = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\frac{1}{\pi'_{0k}}(1-T'_k)Y'_k$. These are identities for every assignment, so the totaled and untotaled HT estimators of $Y_1^T$ and $Y_0^T$, and hence of $\Delta$, coincide.
